title: Used Claude to build an algo off my real life trading (scalping SPY options) and it started out performing me.
author: Four_0_one_k
selftext:
In July, the first full month, it made $36k in profit and never bought more than 15 contracts, 2 - 6 0dte ATM trades per session. I used TradingView to build the script to monitor its would-be trades while I traded for several months. I wrote a dynamic log and P&L tool baked in. Feel free to utilize it. It’s open source, and is a good jumping-off point for anyone developing their own scalping tool:

https://www.tradingview.com/script/cHRRX51d-0dte-scalper-v4-Kalman-SuperTrend-and-ADX-Volatility-Waves/

replies.author: Four_0_one_k
replies.body:
The one I made will work on all intervals, but best on the 5 minute chart. 

The indicators I used are:

MACD Custom Indicator by ChrisMoody  
Squeeze Momentum Indicator by LazyBear  
Pure Price Action by LuxAlgo  
ADX Volatility Waves by BOSWaves  
SuperTrend AI by LuxAlgo

Good luck!

replies.author: Four_0_one_k
replies.body:
I learned to trade options with a fidelity account. But they don’t have an MCP offering, so I set up RH account for the algo. I move money every couple of weeks from RH -> Fido, and annually to my advisor at JP Morgan. Not looking for props, just sharing my experience. Put the indicator up and watch the SPY on Monday. Let me know how many winning trades and losing trades there are? Welcome the feedback. 

Also, I’m not an avid contributor on Reddit, but what’s the benefit of someone making fake account pictures?

comments.author: Queasy-Yesterday9202
comments.body: Impressive, question on execution. TradingView can't place options orders itself, so what's your path from alert to fill? Are you manually clicking in your broker when the 5-min signal fires, or webhooking to something like a broker API bridge? What's your typical slippage between the signal price and your actual option fill on ATM 0dte. Also is the $36k from broker fills or from the script's built-in P&L log? Asking because the logger tracks "would-be" trades and I'm trying to figure out how close would-be gets to real.
